mechanism: Both drugs cause potassium retention (spironolactone) and loss (chlorthalidone) with opposing effects on electrolytes, plus additive diuretic and hypotensive effects increasing risk of hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, and dehydration.
action: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure closely; adjust doses based on electrolyte levels; educate patient on dietary potassium intake and signs of hyperkalemia.
